subject: Renewal request — GPU credit sculpting plan for Helix Labs
messages:
From: Samir Patel <ops@helixlabs.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:34 -0400
Subject: Renewal: GPU credit sculpting plan for Helix Labs

Rafael —

Thanks for the quick chat earlier. We pulled together the usage exports for Apr–May and attached the run-rate CSV. In short:

- We have predictable base inference traffic (~220 tokens/sec equivalent) but multi-hour nightly batch jobs (fine-tuning / evaluation) cause 60–90 minute spikes where utilization jumps to ~7–8x baseline.
- Our current reserved commit covers typical daytime production but is frequently exhausted during the nightly windows, causing throttling and queued requests.
- We’re up for renewal in July and want to avoid overpaying while keeping the app stable during experimental batch runs.

Can Redwood propose a renewal/expansion approach that:
1) protects production latency during spikes without committing to a full 2–3x permanent increase;
2) defines a clear phased addition so we can budget; and
3) includes an ops playbook for emergency burst (how fast can we add capacity / fall back to cheaper variants?).

Attached: helix_usage_runrate_apr-may-2027.csv

Thanks — Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform Ops, Helix Labs
ops@helixlabs.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:03:20 -0400
Subject: Re: Renewal: GPU credit sculpting plan for Helix Labs

Hi Samir —

Appreciate the data. I skimmed the CSV and a few things jump out — nightly spikes are both high magnitude and consistent in timing, which makes them easier to mitigate without a large permanent uplift.

High-level recommendation (we’ll follow with a formal proposal and a short MAP):

- Phase A (0–3 months): Add a small reserved buffer of 8 A100-equivalent slots dedicated to the Helix production pool during the renewal term. This is sized to eliminate queueing for the 95th percentile of your nightly spikes while keeping daytime costs close to today.
- Phase B (3–9 months): After monitoring, convert 50% of the buffer to on-demand burst credits (lower cost if unused) while keeping autoscale-enabled slots for sustained growth.
- Fallback & routing: Configure policy to route non-latency-sensitive batch jobs to a lower-cost quantized variant, and set a hard latency SLO escape hatch that will failover to a cached/rescore-only path if token latency crosses threshold.

I’ve attached a proposed GPU sculpt matrix (proposed_gpu_sculpt_matrix_v1.xlsx) with slot counts, equivalent A100 numbers, and estimated monthly delta to the commit. Ben, Karthik — can you validate the technical assumptions (batch scheduling window and quantized variant impact) and confirm the deployment timeline for a phased addition?

I’ll put a short mutual action plan (MAP) in a doc and share a DocuSign-ready amendment once we align on counts.

Best,
Rafael Mendes

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 08:45:09 -0400
Subject: Re: Renewal: GPU credit sculpting plan for Helix Labs

Rafael / team —

Quick tech note after reviewing their traces (thanks Samir for the CSV):

- Pattern: ~90% of spike volume is concentrated in a 45–80 minute window starting ~02:20 local. Bursts show high seq lengths driven by evaluation workloads, not steady chat traffic.
- Impact: The platform’s autoscaler currently reacts to token-level queueing after ~30s; by then some jobs are already degraded.

Practical mitigation we can deliver quickly:
1) Elastic sculpting pool: carve out 8 dedicated slots for the renewal term and enable short-lived preemptible slices that can be spun up in <90s via our burst API for repeatable nightly runs.
2) Quantized eval path: offer a quantized variant of the customer model for batch evaluation that reduces GPU time by ~40% with minimal quality loss; add route-level toggle to silently prefer quantized for scheduled runs.
3) Canary & observability: instrument a short-lived canary job to run the heaviest nightly job against the quantized path during week 1 post-deploy to validate quality.

Estimate: incremental committed monthly cost for Phase A = ~$12k/mo (8 A100-equiv). If they prefer lower committed spend, we can shift to 6 committed + 4 burst credits (slightly more ops work, slightly higher expected run cost).

Operational timeline (assuming contract signed):
- T+0–2 days: sign amendment & provisioning ticket
- T+2–5 days: provision dedicated slots + route toggles
- T+5–14 days: observability checks, canary runs, and ops playbook handover

Samir — would you prefer the more conservative 6+4 burst model or the simpler 8-commit approach?

—Ben
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

Thanks — this is exactly the kind of pragmatic plan we wanted. We prefer the 6 committed + 4 burst credits model to start (keeps our committed dollar exposure lower while giving the ops buffer). Please:

- Add the 6+4 option to the MAP and include the monthly estimated delta vs current commit.
- Include a one-page ops playbook for the on-call engineer (how to trigger bursts, how to toggle quantized path, rollback steps).
- We will need a 30-day review milestone in the MAP to revisit conversion to more committed slots if nightly jobs remain high.

Marissa / Rafael — please share the updated MAP and send the amendment/DocuSign link when ready. Billing is on cc — they’ll need the final numbers for procurement.

Samir
